documents.title: Read the audio tour
documents.text: Each numbered stop on the audio tour has a transcript. Scan the stop marker, open the Transcript tab and enlarge the text if needed. The front desk has a large-print booklet with the same narration.

documents.title: Borrow a listening receiver
documents.text: Visitors can borrow a portable receiver for the audio tour at the front desk. Pair the receiver with a neckloop and select the stop number. A staff member can replay the narration at a comfortable volume.

documents.title: Add subtitles to the cinema
documents.text: The projection desk can enable captions for the film in the small cinema. Check the subtitle track on the projector before doors open. The film captions describe speech and relevant sound.

documents.title: Reset an audio stop tablet
documents.text: When a stop tablet is blank, check the audio tour app is open and the screen power is on. Use the staff reset card to restart that exhibit. The tablet displays the stop marker and its transcript after restart.

documents.title: Move a timed admission
documents.text: Open the ticket booking and use Change visit to move unused admissions to a later date. Keep the same ticket type. The original entry code becomes invalid after rebooking, and the new code is shown on the confirmation page.

documents.title: Find an admission code
documents.text: The confirmation email shows a square entry code for each timed admission. If the booking email is missing, the front desk can look up the ticket using the last name and visit date. A replacement code must be sent to the original booking address.

documents.title: Handle a double charge
documents.text: If two card payments appear for one ticket booking, check whether one is still pending. Send confirmed duplicate charges to the admissions supervisor with the two receipt references. The admissions supervisor starts the refund against the original payment method.

documents.title: Recover at the entry scanner
documents.text: If the ticket scanner shows already used, check the entry history before issuing a replacement code. A code can be used once. For a gate reader fault, take the admission confirmation to the staffed front desk.

documents.title: Step-free entrance to the upper gallery
documents.text: Enter by the courtyard ramp and take the lift to level two. There are no steps between the courtyard doors and the lift. Wide turning space is available outside the upper gallery.

documents.title: Keep a route open during lift maintenance
documents.text: When the public lift is closed for maintenance, move the level-two talks to the ground-floor studio. Mark the courtyard route on the board and tell the front desk which sessions moved. Keep the service lift for staff.

documents.title: Plan a quiet visit
documents.text: The first Saturday session lowers the gallery volume and leaves the lights steady. The study room is a quiet place to pause. Visitors can step out of a talk and return using the same admission.

documents.title: Hand over found property
documents.text: Tag found belongings with the place and time, then take them to the duty desk. The lost property register records the description and shelf. Never keep a found phone or wallet in the gallery office.

documents.title: Collect a lost item
documents.text: The duty desk releases registered property after the claimant describes it without prompting. Check the shelf record, close the register entry and record the collection time. Valuable belongings stay locked until collection.

documents.title: Return borrowed umbrellas
documents.text: Put borrowed umbrellas into the rack by the courtyard doors. Wipe the handle and let the canopy dry before lending it out again. An umbrella left behind by a visitor goes to the duty desk as found property.

documents.title: Prepare a school workshop
documents.text: The education host checks the class size and adult count in the workshop booking. Set out group workstations and printed activity sheets before the teacher arrives. Escort the group from the courtyard to the studio together.

documents.title: Move a group lunch indoors
documents.text: In heavy rain the schools host opens the studio for packed lunches. Move the workshop trolleys out and place a cleaning kit near the door. Let the teacher know where the group can leave bags during lunch.

documents.title: Restore the booking register
documents.text: If the booking register is damaged, copy the last verified backup into a temporary workspace. Compare the restored visit count and latest ticket reference before releasing the restored register. Keep the damaged copy for investigation.

documents.title: Keep admitting visitors during an outage
documents.text: When the booking service is offline, use the current day's printed admission list. Record arrivals and manually reconcile them when the service returns. Do not issue refunds or new tickets against the offline list.

cases.question: How can a visitor read the narration instead of listening at a stop?
cases.why: The printed booklet and on-screen transcript both contain the stop narration.

cases.question: Which subtitle track should I turn on at the projector?
cases.why: The cinema procedure covers switching on captions for the projected film.

cases.question: Can I push my entry booking back?
cases.why: The timed admission procedure describes moving the visit and replacing its entry code.

cases.question: My confirmation email is missing and my replacement code shows already used.
cases.why: One procedure covers finding the original booking. The other checks a used code before replacing it.

cases.question: How do I reach the upstairs exhibition without stairs?
cases.why: The courtyard ramp and lift provide a step-free route to the upper gallery.

cases.question: A visitor left a wallet. How do I record it and give it back?
cases.why: The handover procedure records found items and the collection procedure covers their release.

cases.question: Where can pupils eat their sandwiches if it pours?
cases.why: The indoor lunch procedure gives a wet-weather space for school groups.

cases.question: How should we admit people while the booking service is offline?
cases.why: The outage procedure uses the printed list until the booking service returns.

cases.question: Someone paid twice for the same ticket. Who handles the refund?
cases.why: The duplicate payment procedure identifies the admissions supervisor.

cases.question: Can I reprint the admission code while the front gate reader is broken?
cases.why: The scanner recovery procedure routes reader faults to the staffed desk.
